data.ruling: The datasheet verifier's refutation stands for the transient half of V112. The value says no page states a transient at the servo converter's VIN or its duration, and records it as not read. Research.md at 68adf31, which this run reads, does state one. Line 591 (Follow-ups, input transient clamp) puts 60 V for 10 us on the input. TVS2701DRBR clamps it to 35.7 V at 27 degC and 37.3 V at 125 degC. Behind the overvoltage cut-off, the bus carries that voltage to the TPS55285 for 3.98 us typical and 5.4 us maximum, plus the MOSFETs' gate-discharge time. V308 (line 1021) gives the owner's answer of 2026-10-02 in its Answer column: a second clamp on the bus, behind the cut-off and ahead of the TPS55285, holds the TPS55285 input pins at or under 27 V. The corrected value reads as follows. Steady: 20 V. Transient at VIN: at most 27 V, held by the owner's second clamp (part not selected). Without that clamp the bus sees 35.7 to 37.3 V for 0.00398 ms typical and 0.0054 ms maximum, plus a gate-discharge time no page states (not read). The steady half holds. Re-read in SLVSI72A (April 2025, revised October 2025), the TPS55285 gives: VIN absolute maximum 27 V (5.1); recommended input range 22 V maximum; VVIN_OVP 22 V min, 22.5 V typ and 23 V max rising, with 0.9 V hysteresis. The refutation concerns this question's requirement value, not the part, so its scope is function.
